coptic_restorations.basis: Editor's proposal confirmed: the title and the immediately following enumeration both name 'five' (ⲡϯⲟⲩ ⲛⲍⲱⲃ). ⲥⲙⲛ̄ + ϯⲟⲩ = 'established five [great things],' anticipating the five-item list. Lexicon: ϯⲟⲩ (five) as the structural articulation at the rational/natural interface.

Editor's proposal confirmed. The trace ⲛ̄ⲁⲛⲧⲉⲗ- needs final ⲙ to give ⲁⲛⲧⲉⲗⲙ (canal/conduit), then ⲍⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'in the bodies' restores the title's locative ('in the bodies of the archons'). Parallels the preceding ⲙ̄ⲙⲟⲟⲙⲉ 'veins.'

ⲁⲭⲛ requires a following article before ⲍⲃⲉ ('shoulder,' fem.). The standard Manichaean formula is simply 'upon the shoulder of the Omophoros' (cf. lexicon: Omophoros = the bearing-up principle). The article ⲧ- completes ⲁⲭⲛ ⲧⲍⲃⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲙⲟⲫⲟⲣⲟⲥ.
Trace ⲧⲧⲙ̄...ⲩ + position 'second' in the enumeration → ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ ('the second'). Parallels ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ (1919, fourth) and ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϯⲟⲩ (1922, fifth). Lexicon: ⲥⲛⲉⲩ = 'two.'

ⲙ̄ + article + ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ in next segment → ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ 'of the Pillar.' This is the Pillar of Glory (path of regeneration in the lexicon: ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ), described in the reading as 'stretched forth through the very midst' — confirmed by ⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲡⲉϩⲙⲏⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.
Trace …ⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ + 'third' position in enumeration → ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ('the third'). Parallels ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ (second), ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ (fourth), ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϯⲟⲩ (fifth). Lexicon: ϣⲁⲙⲧ = 'three.'

Gap straddles the line break between ⲡ at end of 1917 and ⲙⲁ at start of 1918, yielding the natural reading ⲡⲙⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ 'the place of the molding/formation' — matching the spiritual reading ('the Lord's shaping hand on the formation of the lowest states'). The marked gap appears to be a line-break artifact of damage rather than missing letters; no further fill is securely warranted.

Trace ⲡⲙⲟⲩ…ⲛ̄ⲕ resolves directly to ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ ('molding/formation,' lexicon: ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ = form/build/mold), with no medial letters required. The marked gap is internal damage to a single intact word; no actual letters are missing in the lexical reconstruction.

Exact parallel with section 1922 fifth-item formula ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϯⲟⲩ ⲡⲉ ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲃⲧ̄ ('the fifth is the four walls'). Here: ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲡⲉ ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ('the fourth is the four pillars'). The ⲛ̄ is already preserved at the head of segment 1920. Lexicon: ϩⲧⲁⲩ = 'four,' fullness in extension; reading: 'the four supporting pillars whose feet stand in the great mass of natural perception.'

ⲍⲛ̄ + article + ⲥⲁϣϩⲉ ('seventh-fem.') in next segment → ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲁϣϩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'in the seventh kind of the cosmos.' The ordinal prefix ⲧⲙⲁⲍ- is the standard Lycopolitan formation, mirroring the ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍ- ordinals throughout the teaching.

english_restorations.basis: Direct lexical correlate of the restored ϯⲟⲩ: the teaching enumerates exactly five works, and the title likewise names 'the Five Things.'

Translates the restored ⲍⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁ; matches the title's locative ('in the bodies of the strong archons') — the natural mind as the self has organized it, through which the Living Spirit's structural supports run.

Translates the restored ϩⲧⲁⲩ ('four'); parallels the fifth item ('the four walls') and matches the spiritual reading: 'the four supporting pillars whose feet stand in the great mass of natural perception.'

restoration_note: The teaching enumerates five structural supports the Living Spirit (the Lord's operative power) established within the bodies of the self-archons: (1) the disc on the Omophoros' shoulder, (2) the foreparts of the Pillar of Glory stretched through the midst, (3) the place of the molding of the Gehennas, (4) four pillars set in the great sea at the seventh stratum of the cosmos, (5) four walls surrounding the strongholds. The strong parallel structure of the ordinal formulas ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍ- + numeral, the explicit fifth-item parallel (ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲃⲧ̄), and the lexicon's terms for Omophoros, Pillar of Glory, and stronghold tightly constrained ordinal prefixes ({3},{5},{8},{9}), the editor's enumeration ({0},{1}), and the article-fills ({2},{4}). Two gaps ({6},{7}) are line-break/internal damage artifacts in the secure phrase ⲡⲙⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ 'the place of the molding,' where the surrounding traces leave no securely missing letters; both marked unrestorable rather than padded.
